In [[geometry]], the '''augmented dodecahedron''' is a [[Johnson solid]] combining a [[regular dodecahedron]] and a [[pentagonal pyramid]].
[[File:J58 augmented dodecahedron.stl|thumb|3D model of an augmented dodecahedron]]

== Construction ==
An augmented dodecahedron is constructed from a [[regular dodecahedron]], a twelve-sided polyhedron with regular pentagons, by attaching a regular-faced [[pentagonal pyramid]] to one of the regular dodecahedron's faces; the regular polygons mean that all of its internal angles and edges are equal. The resulting polyhedron covers one pentagon from a dodecahedron with five equilateral triangles from the pyramid. Ergo, the augmented dodecahedron has eleven pentagonal faces and five equilateral triangular faces, totaling sixteen faces.{{r|berman}} The augmented is [[Johnson solid]], a convex polyhedron with regular faces, enumerated as the fifty-eighth <math> J_{58} </math>.{{r|francis}}

== Properties ==
The surface area of an augmented dodecahedron <math> A </math> is obtained by summing the area of its faces, eleven regular pentagons and five equilateral triangles. Its volume <math> V </math> is obtained by adding the volume of a regular dodecahedron and a pentagonal pyramid, as suggested by the construction:{{r|berman}}
<math display="block">
\begin{align}
 A &= 11 \cdot \frac{{\sqrt {25 + 10\sqrt 5} }}{4}a^2 + 5 \cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^2 \approx 21.09a^2, \\
 V &= \frac{15 + 7\sqrt{5}}{4}a^3 + \frac{5 + \sqrt{5}}{24} a^3 \approx 7.965a^3.
\end{align} </math>
